title: The SIRIC Study (Systemic Inflammatory Response in Cardiac Intensive Care): A prospective analysis of the systemic inflammation and its impact on perioperative outcomes in cardiac intensive care patients
summary: After cardiac surgery or during mechanical circulatory support, patients may develop varying degrees of inflammation throughout the body. The aim of this observational study is to better understand these inflammatory responses using blood and urine analyses and to investigate their relationship with clinical outcomes. Blood samples and, where available, urine samples will be collected at several time points, and clinical data will be recorded. All patients will receive standard medical care independent of study participation. In the long term, the study aims to improve the early identification of patients at increased risk of complications and support more personalized intensive care management.

interventions.name: Prospective observational study in adult patients (≥18 years) admitted to the cardiac intensive care unit following cardiac surgery or for mechanical circulatory support (MCS).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) Admission to the cardiac intensive care unit following cardiac surgery or for treatment with mechanical circulatory support (MCS).
2) Written informed consent provided by the patient or a legally authorized representative in accordance with applicable legal requirements.
Exclusion criteria:
1) Lack of valid informed consent.
2) Participation in another clinical study if this is expected to introduce relevant confounding factors or bias for the present study; assessed on a case-by-case basis by the investigators.
